agent_responses.message: Hi, this is Emma from Atlas Web Studio. I had Acme Dental down as a dental clinic in Phoenix. Am I speaking with the owner or someone who handles the website there?
Yes, that's me. I'm the owner. I was calling about adding some features to the website.
Got it. What kind of features are you thinking about adding?
Yeah, I was thinking about adding online booking, maybe some kind of CRM, and payments.
Yes, we can build that. It depends whether you need a simple form handoff or a real integration. Is this for a new site or an addition to your existing site?
It's for my existing site.

For an existing site, online booking can be simple if it is just appointment requests, or integrated if it needs a live calendar. Payments and CRM depend on whether data needs to move automatically between systems.
So, which one is better, or what's the difference for my site?

For your site, the simple option is usually best if you just need patients to request appointments and your team confirms them manually. The integrated option is better if you want live availability, automatic confirmations, payments, or CRM records created without staff retyping details.
Okay, so the integrated option sounds like it does more. What does that involve for my site, exactly?

It usually means connecting the website to the booking, payment, and CRM tools so information moves automatically instead of being handled manually. We would need to scope the exact systems, what data moves, and what should happen after someone books or pays.
So, what's the next step for my site then?
We collect that during scoping if you move forward.
What does "scoping" mean? And what do I need to do to "move forward"?

Scoping means we map out the exact tools, data flow, pages, and user steps before quoting or building anything. To move forward, we would first understand what you want connected and then decide whether it is a simple handoff or a real integration.

agent_responses.message: Hi, this is Emma from Atlas Web Studio. I had Acme Dental down as a dental clinic in Phoenix. Am I speaking with the owner or someone who handles the website there?
Yeah, that's me. I was calling to ask about how much a basic three-to-five-page site costs.
A basic three-to-five-page new site is usually nine hundred to fifteen hundred dollars. The driver is how much content and layout customization you need.
So what's the difference between the nine hundred and fifteen hundred, then?

The lower end is usually a straightforward brochure-style site with standard sections and content you already have. The higher end is for more custom layout work, extra content shaping, or more back-and-forth to get the pages right.
So, if I need help writing the words for the site, that's the higher price then?
Usually, yes. If we’re helping shape or write the page content instead of just placing content you already have, that tends to push it toward the higher end.
Okay, so if I need you to write the content, it's definitely going to be fifteen hundred?
Not definitely. It depends how much content needs to be written and how much structure is already clear, but content help is one of the things that can move it toward the higher end.
So, what's the most it would be if I need help with the words?
For a basic three-to-five-page site, the range is still nine hundred to fifteen hundred dollars. If the content needs a lot of writing and shaping, it would likely be near the top of that range.

agent_responses.message: Hi, this is Emma from Atlas Web Studio. I had Acme Dental down as a dental clinic in Phoenix. Am I speaking with the owner or someone who handles the website there?
Yeah, that's me. I'm calling about getting a new website.

Perfect. We’re offering a free homepage mockup so you can see what a refreshed site could look like before deciding anything. For a dental clinic, we’d usually focus the homepage around trust, services, location, and a clear way for patients to request an appointment. Would it be okay if I sent one over for Acme Dental?
Uh, yeah, a mockup sounds fine. But I really just need to know how much a simple site with a form would cost.

For a simple new three to five page website with a contact or appointment request form, it’s usually nine hundred to fifteen hundred dollars. The main driver is how much content and page structure you need.
Okay, what about if I wanted to integrate a live calendar for scheduling?

A live calendar is the integrated option, because availability has to connect to a scheduling system instead of just sending a request. For a new site with that kind of standard integration, the whole project is usually four thousand to six thousand five hundred dollars.
Whoa, that's a huge difference just for a calendar.

The difference is that a request form just sends the patient’s information, while a live calendar has to connect to availability, rules, confirmations, and sometimes reminders or patient systems. That extra data flow is what changes the scope.
Is there really no cheaper way to get a calendar on there?

If you already use a scheduling tool that provides an embed or booking link, that can be much simpler than a direct integration. The custom cost comes in when the site has to control availability or sync data directly with another system.
So, if I have a scheduling tool already, it would be closer to the nine hundred to fifteen hundred dollar range?

That’s right, if it’s just a standard embed or booking link on a new simple site, it usually stays closer to the simple-site scope. If it needs custom syncing or patient-system integration, that’s when it becomes a larger project.
Okay, so if I just use my existing scheduling tool, it'll be around that $900 to $1500 price?
That’s right.
Alright, got it. So with my own scheduling tool, it's the lower price. Thanks, bye.

agent_responses.message: Hi, this is Emma from Atlas Web Studio. I had Acme Dental down as a dental clinic in Phoenix. Am I speaking with the owner or someone who handles the website there?

So, if it's WordPress, what's the actual price then? What does that "quick look" cost?
For a compatible WordPress site, a simple appointment request form is usually one hundred to two hundred fifty dollars. The quick look is just to confirm the setup before quoting the exact amount.

We collect the CRM name, the forms or actions involved, the fields that need to pass through, and whether the site needs any data back from the CRM. If you want, the first step here is I can send over the free homepage mockup, and you can reply with those CRM details if it looks useful.

agent_responses.message: Hi, this is Emma from Atlas Web Studio. I had Acme Dental down as a dental clinic in Phoenix. Am I speaking with the owner or someone who handles the website there?
Yeah, I handle the website. What's up?

Great. I’m reaching out because we’re putting together a free homepage mockup for a few local businesses, just a visual concept of how the site could look cleaner and make it easier for patients to take the next step. If it looks useful, you can reply to the email, and if not, there’s no obligation. Would you be open to me sending one over?
Uh, sure, I guess. What's the catch?
No payment or contract.
Okay, but what about monthly hosting and maintenance?
Hosting and maintenance is seventy nine dollars per month.
Seventy-nine dollars? What all does that include?
It covers hosting, basic maintenance, security updates, and keeping the site running properly.
What does "basic maintenance" actually cover?

Basic maintenance means routine platform and plugin updates, uptime monitoring, backups, and small technical fixes needed to keep the site stable. It does not mean ongoing redesigns or new feature development.
So if a page breaks or something stops working, is that covered?
Yes, if something breaks from normal site maintenance or a technical issue, that is generally covered. If it is a new feature, redesign, or a larger content change, that would be scoped separately.
What does "generally covered" mean? Is it always covered or not?
It means routine technical fixes tied to keeping the site stable are covered, but issues caused by new custom work, third party service changes, or larger feature changes may need separate scoping.
So, if something breaks because of your updates, it's covered, but if I change something, it's not?
That's right.

That's right.
